name: Zinc PCA

card.summary: Zinc PCA is the zinc salt of pyrrolidone carboxylic acid, used in cosmetic serums and shampoos to calm shine and oiliness and support clearer, more matte-looking skin.
card.aka: zinc pyrrolidone carboxylate; zinc L-pyrrolidone carboxylate
card.note: Studied mainly inside multi-ingredient creams rather than alone.

quick.overview:
Zinc PCA combines zinc with PCA (pyrrolidone carboxylic acid), a component of the skin's natural moisturizing factor. Cosmetic brands include it as an 'antiseborrheic' or sebum-regulating ingredient in serums, cleansers and scalp products.

The appearance payoff people look for is less visible oiliness and shine, a more matte complexion and a calmer scalp.
quick.how: It is applied as a leave-on serum or cream, or in wash-off cleansers and shampoos, often alongside niacinamide or other oil-control actives. Brands list it in their ingredients; routines are typically daily.
quick.risks: As a cosmetic ingredient it is generally well tolerated in the studies that include it, though sensitive skin can react to any product. Studied formulas combined several active ingredients, so effects cannot be attributed to zinc PCA alone.

lead: Zinc PCA is the zinc salt of pyrrolidone carboxylic acid. PCA itself is a natural amino acid derivative that is part of the skin's natural moisturizing factor, and its sodium salt is a common humectant in skin and hair products [1]. Zinc PCA is added to cosmetics for its antiseborrheic, or oil-regulating, role [2].

In practice it appears in oil-control serums and in anti-dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis formulas. Published trials have tested creams and scalp products containing zinc PCA together with piroctone olamine and other actives, in facial seborrheic dermatitis [3][4], scalp seborrheic dermatitis [5], cradle cap in infants [6] and HIV-positive patients with facial seborrheic dermatitis [7].

chain: Zinc salt added to skincare or scalp products
Sebum-related shine and flaking are reduced
angle.text: Zinc PCA is used in leave-on and wash-off products to cut visible oiliness and support a clearer, more matte complexion or a less flaky scalp.

paras: PCA is also called 5-oxoproline and forms when glutamic acid or glutamine cyclises; it is a humectant component of the natural moisturizing factor [1]. Zinc PCA pairs zinc with PCA and is labelled in studies as the antiseborrheic component of formulas [2].
Cosmetic products with zinc PCA target oily skin and seborrheic dermatitis, a condition involving Malassezia yeasts, hormones and sebum levels [3].

Studies tested multi-ingredient products, so results reflect the combination. In 20 adults with mild-to-moderate facial seborrheic dermatitis, a cream containing piroctone olamine, stearyl glycyrrhetinate and zinc PCA was applied twice daily for 60 days and assessed by clinical and instrumental measures [4]. A case series of 11 patients tested a non-steroidal facial cream [3]. A 4-week study of 20 patients combined a salicylic acid, piroctone olamine and zinc PCA scalp gel with a cleansing lotion [5]. A 30-day open trial in 10 infants with cradle cap used a gel cream containing zinc PCA [6], and a 12-week pilot in 20 HIV-positive patients used a similar cream [7]. All were small, open-label designs.
